description:
Section G — Algorithm and Parameter Choice (private-CA trust scope).

CustomCaTransport::build_client() at crate-jmap-base-client/src/auth.rs:74-83 calls reqwest::ClientBuilder::add_root_certificate(cert) without first calling tls_built_in_root_certs(false). Per reqwest 0.12 documentation, add_root_certificate ADDS the certificate to the existing trust roots (webpki-roots) — it does not replace them.

The likely user-mental-model for CustomCaTransport is 'connect to a JMAP server identified by a private CA we control, refusing certificates signed by any public CA.' That is the threat model where private-CA pinning matters: a corporate internal JMAP server, a service-mesh deployment, an air-gapped network. Under the current behavior, a connection to this server will be accepted if the server presents a certificate signed by EITHER the configured private CA OR any of the 100+ public CAs in webpki-roots. A compromised or malicious public CA (Symantec 2017, DigiNotar 2011, etc.) issuing a certificate for the target host name therefore bypasses the private-CA defense entirely.

# What goes wrong (confidentiality/integrity)

A consumer that intentionally configured a private CA expecting trust isolation gets neither isolation nor a compile-time/runtime signal that the isolation is incomplete. Mis-issued public-CA certs or compromised intermediates can MITM the TLS connection, recovering credentials (BearerAuth/BasicAuth in the Authorization header) and full session content.

# Suggested fix

Two options:

1) Default to replace: in CustomCaTransport::build_client, call .tls_built_in_root_certs(false) before .add_root_certificate(cert). This matches the likely user mental model. Document the change in the rustdoc.

2) Make it explicit: add a #[non_exhaustive] field like include_public_roots: bool (default false) to CustomCaTransport and route through both reqwest builder calls. The downside is a SemVer-additive shape change.

Either way, the rustdoc on CustomCaTransport currently says 'Custom CA trust root (DER-encoded). No Authorization header is injected.' — it never tells the reader that the public webpki-roots remain in the trust set. The current behaviour is documented nowhere and is opposite to the likely expectation.

# Probe (read-only)

Verify by reading reqwest 0.12 ClientBuilder source for add_root_certificate vs tls_built_in_root_certs. The author of reqwest documents both methods in the same module — add_root_certificate adds, tls_built_in_root_certs(false) disables the bundled defaults. The fix is mechanical.

# Test discipline

After implementing the fix, a defense-in-depth integration test can verify by spinning up two wiremock servers — one with a webpki-rooted cert (legitimate public CA), one with the configured private CA — and asserting the public-CA host is REJECTED (TLS handshake failure) while the private-CA host is accepted. Test fixture certs from rcgen or similar.

# References

- reqwest 0.12 ClientBuilder docs: add_root_certificate, tls_built_in_root_certs
- Workspace AGENTS.md 'TLS stack' rule pins rustls; this finding does not change that — it changes how the rustls trust root configuration is composed.
title: CustomCaTransport ADDS to default trust roots; cannot restrict trust to private CA only
